content.latin: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us adore.

segments.t: Ant.
Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

segments.t: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius

veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.

Regem Apostolórum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.

segments.t: Ant.
Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

content.latin: 18:2 Cæli enárrant glóriam Dei: * et ópera mánuum eius annúntiat firmaméntum.
content.english: 18:2 The heavens shew forth the glory of God, * and the firmament declareth the work of his hands.

segments.t: Cæli enárrant glóriam Dei: * et ópera mánuum eius annúntiat firmaméntum.

content.latin: 18:3 Dies diéi erúctat verbum, * et nox nocti índicat sciéntiam.
content.english: 18:3 Day to day uttereth speech, * and night to night sheweth knowledge.

segments.t: Dies diéi erúctat verbum, * et nox nocti índicat sciéntiam.

content.latin: 18:4 Non sunt loquélæ, neque sermónes, * quorum non audiántur voces eórum.
content.english: 18:4 There are no speeches nor languages, * where their voices are not heard.

segments.t: Non sunt loquélæ, neque sermónes, * quorum non audiántur voces eórum.

content.latin: 18:5 In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum: * et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.
content.english: 18:5 Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth: * and their words unto the ends of the world.

segments.t: In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum: * et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.

content.latin: 18:6 In sole pósuit tabernáculum suum: * et ipse tamquam sponsus procédens de thálamo suo:
content.english: 18:6 He hath set his tabernacle in the sun: * and he, as a bridegroom coming out of his bride chamber,

segments.t: In sole pósuit tabernáculum suum: * et ipse tamquam sponsus procédens de thálamo suo:

content.latin: 18:6 Exsultávit ut gigas ad curréndam viam, * a summo cælo egréssio eius:
content.english: 18:6 Hath rejoiced as a giant to run the way: * his going out is from the end of heaven,

segments.t: Exsultávit ut gigas ad curréndam viam, * a summo cælo egréssio eius:

content.latin: 18:7 Et occúrsus eius usque ad summum eius: * nec est qui se abscóndat a calóre eius.
content.english: 18:7 And his circuit even to the end thereof: * and there is no one that can hide himself from his heat.

segments.t: Et occúrsus eius usque ad summum eius: * nec est qui se abscóndat a calóre eius.

content.latin: 18:8 Lex Dómini immaculáta, convértens ánimas: * testimónium Dómini fidéle, sapiéntiam præstans párvulis.
content.english: 18:8 The law of the Lord is unspotted, converting souls: * the testimony of the Lord is faithful, giving wisdom to little ones.

segments.t: Lex Dómini immaculáta, convértens ánimas: * testimónium Dómini fidéle, sapiéntiam præstans párvulis.

content.latin: 18:9 Iustítiæ Dómini rectæ, lætificántes corda: * præcéptum Dómini lúcidum, illúminans óculos.
content.english: 18:9 The justices of the Lord are right, rejoicing hearts: * the commandment of the Lord is lightsome, enlightening the eyes.

segments.t: Iustítiæ Dómini rectæ, lætificántes corda: * præcéptum Dómini lúcidum, illúminans óculos.

content.latin: 18:10 Timor Dómini sanctus, pérmanens in sǽculum sǽculi: * iudícia Dómini vera, iustificáta in semetípsa.
content.english: 18:10 The fear of the Lord is holy, enduring for ever and ever: * the judgments of the Lord are true, justified in themselves.

segments.t: Timor Dómini sanctus, pérmanens in sǽculum sǽculi: * iudícia Dómini vera, iustificáta in semetípsa.

content.latin: 18:11 Desiderabília super aurum et lápidem pretiósum multum: * et dulcióra super mel et favum.
content.english: 18:11 More to be desired than gold and many precious stones: * and sweeter than honey and the honeycomb.

segments.t: Desiderabília super aurum et lápidem pretiósum multum: * et dulcióra super mel et favum.

content.latin: 18:12 Étenim servus tuus custódit ea, * in custodiéndis illis retribútio multa.
content.english: 18:12 For thy servant keepeth them, * and in keeping them there is a great reward.

segments.t: Étenim servus tuus custódit ea, * in custodiéndis illis retribútio multa.

content.latin: 18:13 Delícta quis intéllegit? ab occúltis meis munda me: * et ab aliénis parce servo tuo.
content.english: 18:13 Who can understand sins? from my secret ones cleanse me, O Lord: * and from those of others spare thy servant.

segments.t: Delícta quis intéllegit? ab occúltis meis munda me: * et ab aliénis parce servo tuo.

content.latin: 18:14 Si mei non fúerint domináti, tunc immaculátus ero: * et emundábor a delícto máximo.
content.english: 18:14 If they shall have no dominion over me, then shall I be without spot: * and I shall be cleansed from the greatest sin.

segments.t: Si mei non fúerint domináti, tunc immaculátus ero: * et emundábor a delícto máximo.

content.latin: 18:15 Et erunt ut compláceant elóquia oris mei: * et meditátio cordis mei in conspéctu tuo semper.
content.english: 18:15 And the words of my mouth shall be such as may please: * and the meditation of my heart always in thy sight.

segments.t: Et erunt ut compláceant elóquia oris mei: * et meditátio cordis mei in conspéctu tuo semper.

content.latin: 18:15 Dómine, adiútor meus, * et redémptor meus.
content.english: 18:15 O Lord, my helper, * and my redeemer.

segments.t: Dómine, adiútor meus, * et redémptor meus.

content.latin: Psalmus 33 [2]
content.english: Psalm 33 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 33

content.latin: 33:2 Benedícam Dóminum in omni témpore: * semper laus eius in ore meo.
content.english: 33:2 I will bless the Lord at all times, * his praise shall be always in my mouth.

segments.t: Benedícam Dóminum in omni témpore: * semper laus eius in ore meo.

content.latin: 33:3 In Dómino laudábitur ánima mea: * áudiant mansuéti, et læténtur.
content.english: 33:3 In the Lord shall my soul be praised: * let the meek hear and rejoice.

segments.t: In Dómino laudábitur ánima mea: * áudiant mansuéti, et læténtur.

content.latin: 33:4 Magnificáte Dóminum mecum: * et exaltémus nomen eius in idípsum.
content.english: 33:4 O magnify the Lord with me; * and let us extol his name together.

segments.t: Magnificáte Dóminum mecum: * et exaltémus nomen eius in idípsum.

content.latin: 33:5 Exquisívi Dóminum, et exaudívit me: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus meis erípuit me.
content.english: 33:5 I sought the Lord, and he heard me; * and he delivered me from all my troubles.

segments.t: Exquisívi Dóminum, et exaudívit me: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus meis erípuit me.

content.latin: 33:6 Accédite ad eum, et illuminámini: * et fácies vestræ non confundéntur.
content.english: 33:6 Come ye to him and be enlightened: * and your faces shall not be confounded.

segments.t: Accédite ad eum, et illuminámini: * et fácies vestræ non confundéntur.

content.latin: 33:7 Iste pauper clamávit, et Dóminus exaudívit eum: * et de ómnibus tribulatiónibus eius salvávit eum.
content.english: 33:7 This poor man cried, and the Lord heard him: * and saved him out of all his troubles.

segments.t: Iste pauper clamávit, et Dóminus exaudívit eum: * et de ómnibus tribulatiónibus eius salvávit eum.

content.latin: 33:8 Immíttet Ángelus Dómini in circúitu timéntium eum: * et erípiet eos.
content.english: 33:8 The Angel of the Lord shall encamp round about them that fear him: * and shall deliver them.

segments.t: Immíttet Ángelus Dómini in circúitu timéntium eum: * et erípiet eos.

content.latin: 33:9 Gustáte, et vidéte quóniam suávis est Dóminus: * beátus vir, qui sperat in eo.
content.english: 33:9 O taste, and see that the Lord is sweet: * blessed is the man that hopeth in him.

segments.t: Gustáte, et vidéte quóniam suávis est Dóminus: * beátus vir, qui sperat in eo.

content.latin: 33:10 Timéte Dóminum, omnes sancti eius: * quóniam non est inópia timéntibus eum.
content.english: 33:10 Fear the Lord, all ye his saints: * for there is no want to them that fear him.

segments.t: Timéte Dóminum, omnes sancti eius: * quóniam non est inópia timéntibus eum.

content.latin: 33:11 Dívites eguérunt et esuriérunt: * inquiréntes autem Dóminum non minuéntur omni bono.
content.english: 33:11 The rich have wanted, and have suffered hunger: * but they that seek the Lord shall not be deprived of any good.

segments.t: Dívites eguérunt et esuriérunt: * inquiréntes autem Dóminum non minuéntur omni bono.

content.latin: 33:12 Veníte, fílii, audíte me: * timórem Dómini docébo vos.
content.english: 33:12 Come, children, hearken to me: * I will teach you the fear of the Lord.

segments.t: Veníte, fílii, audíte me: * timórem Dómini docébo vos.

content.latin: 33:13 Quis est homo qui vult vitam: * díligit dies vidére bonos?
content.english: 33:13 Who is the man that desireth life: * who loveth to see good days?

segments.t: Quis est homo qui vult vitam: * díligit dies vidére bonos?

content.latin: 33:14 Próhibe linguam tuam a malo: * et lábia tua ne loquántur dolum.
content.english: 33:14 Keep thy tongue from evil, * and thy lips from speaking guile.

segments.t: Próhibe linguam tuam a malo: * et lábia tua ne loquántur dolum.

content.latin: 33:15 Divérte a malo, et fac bonum: * inquíre pacem, et perséquere eam.
content.english: 33:15 Turn away from evil and do good: * seek after peace and pursue it.

segments.t: Divérte a malo, et fac bonum: * inquíre pacem, et perséquere eam.

content.latin: 33:16 Óculi Dómini super iustos: * et aures eius in preces eórum.
content.english: 33:16 The eyes of the Lord are upon the just: * and his ears unto their prayers.

segments.t: Óculi Dómini super iustos: * et aures eius in preces eórum.

content.latin: 33:17 Vultus autem Dómini super faciéntes mala: * ut perdat de terra memóriam eórum.
content.english: 33:17 But the countenance of the Lord is against them that do evil things: * to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth.

segments.t: Vultus autem Dómini super faciéntes mala: * ut perdat de terra memóriam eórum.

content.latin: 33:18 Clamavérunt iusti, et Dóminus exaudívit eos: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus eórum liberávit eos.
content.english: 33:18 The just cried, and the Lord heard them: * and delivered them out of all their troubles.

segments.t: Clamavérunt iusti, et Dóminus exaudívit eos: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus eórum liberávit eos.

content.latin: 33:19 Iuxta est Dóminus iis, qui tribuláto sunt corde: * et húmiles spíritu salvábit.
content.english: 33:19 The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a contrite heart: * and he will save the humble of spirit.

segments.t: Iuxta est Dóminus iis, qui tribuláto sunt corde: * et húmiles spíritu salvábit.

content.latin: 33:20 Multæ tribulatiónes iustórum: * et de ómnibus his liberábit eos Dóminus.
content.english: 33:20 Many are the afflictions of the just; * but out of them all will the Lord deliver them.

segments.t: Multæ tribulatiónes iustórum: * et de ómnibus his liberábit eos Dóminus.

content.latin: 33:21 Custódit Dóminus ómnia ossa eórum: * unum ex his non conterétur.
content.english: 33:21 The Lord keepeth all their bones, * not one of them shall be broken.

segments.t: Custódit Dóminus ómnia ossa eórum: * unum ex his non conterétur.

content.latin: 33:22 Mors peccatórum péssima: * et qui odérunt iustum, delínquent.
content.english: 33:22 The death of the wicked is very evil: * and they that hate the just shall be guilty.

segments.t: Mors peccatórum péssima: * et qui odérunt iustum, delínquent.

content.latin: 33:23 Rédimet Dóminus ánimas servórum suórum: * et non delínquent omnes qui sperant in eo.
content.english: 33:23 The Lord will redeem the souls of his servants: * and none of them that trust in him shall offend.

segments.t: Rédimet Dóminus ánimas servórum suórum: * et non delínquent omnes qui sperant in eo.

content.english: Psalm 44 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 44

content.latin: 44:2 Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: * dico ego ópera mea Regi.
content.english: 44:2 My heart hath uttered a good word; * I speak my works to the King.

segments.t: Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: * dico ego ópera mea Regi.

content.latin: 44:2 Lingua mea cálamus scribæ: * velóciter scribéntis.
content.english: 44:2 My tongue is the pen of a scrivener * that writeth swiftly.

segments.t: Lingua mea cálamus scribæ: * velóciter scribéntis.

content.latin: 44:3 Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis: * proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.
content.english: 44:3 Thou art beautiful above the sons of men: grace is poured abroad in thy lips; * therefore hath God blessed thee for ever.

segments.t: Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis: * proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.

content.latin: 44:4 Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, * potentíssime.
content.english: 44:4 Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, * O thou most mighty.

segments.t: Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, * potentíssime.

content.latin: 44:5 Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua: * inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
content.english: 44:5 With thy comeliness and thy beauty * set out, proceed prosperously, and reign.

segments.t: Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua: * inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.

content.latin: 44:5 Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et iustítiam: * et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.
content.english: 44:5 Because of truth and meekness and justice: * and thy right hand shall conduct thee wonderfully.

segments.t: Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et iustítiam: * et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.

content.latin: 44:6 Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ, pópuli sub te cadent: * in corda inimicórum Regis.
content.english: 44:6 Thy arrows are sharp: under thee shall people fall, * into the hearts of the king’s enemies.

segments.t: Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ, pópuli sub te cadent: * in corda inimicórum Regis.

content.latin: 44:7 Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum sǽculi: * virga directiónis virga regni tui.
content.english: 44:7 Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: * the sceptre of thy kingdom is a sceptre of uprightness.

segments.t: Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum sǽculi: * virga directiónis virga regni tui.

content.latin: 44:8 Dilexísti iustítiam, et odísti iniquitátem: * proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ præ consórtibus tuis.
content.english: 44:8 Thou hast loved justice, and hated iniquity: * therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.

segments.t: Dilexísti iustítiam, et odísti iniquitátem: * proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ præ consórtibus tuis.

content.latin: 44:9 Myrrha, et gutta, et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a dómibus ebúrneis: * ex quibus delectavérunt te fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.
content.english: 44:9 Myrrh and stacte and cassia perfume thy garments, from the ivory houses: * out of which the daughters of kings have delighted thee in thy glory.

segments.t: Myrrha, et gutta, et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a dómibus ebúrneis: * ex quibus delectavérunt te fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.

content.latin: 44:10 Ástitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto: * circúmdata varietáte.
content.english: 44:10 The queen stood on thy right hand, in gilded clothing; * surrounded with variety.

segments.t: Ástitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto: * circúmdata varietáte.

content.latin: 44:11 Audi fília, et vide, et inclína aurem tuam: * et oblivíscere pópulum tuum et domum patris tui.
content.english: 44:11 Hearken, O daughter, and see, and incline thy ear: * and forget thy people and thy father’s house.

segments.t: Audi fília, et vide, et inclína aurem tuam: * et oblivíscere pópulum tuum et domum patris tui.

content.latin: 44:12 Et concupíscet Rex decórem tuum: * quóniam ipse est Dóminus Deus tuus, et adorábunt eum.
content.english: 44:12 And the king shall greatly desire thy beauty; * for he is the Lord thy God, and him they shall adore.

segments.t: Et concupíscet Rex decórem tuum: * quóniam ipse est Dóminus Deus tuus, et adorábunt eum.

content.latin: 44:13 Et fíliæ Tyri in munéribus * vultum tuum deprecabúntur: omnes dívites plebis.
content.english: 44:13 And the daughters of Tyre with gifts, * yea, all the rich among the people, shall entreat thy countenance.

segments.t: Et fíliæ Tyri in munéribus * vultum tuum deprecabúntur: omnes dívites plebis.

content.latin: 44:14 Omnis glória eius fíliæ Regis ab intus, * in fímbriis áureis circumamícta varietátibus.
content.english: 44:14 All the glory of the king’s daughter is within, * in golden borders, clothed round about with varieties.

segments.t: Omnis glória eius fíliæ Regis ab intus, * in fímbriis áureis circumamícta varietátibus.

content.latin: 44:15 Adducéntur Regi vírgines post eam: * próximæ eius afferéntur tibi.
content.english: 44:15 After her shall virgins be brought to the king: * her neighbours shall be brought to thee.

segments.t: Adducéntur Regi vírgines post eam: * próximæ eius afferéntur tibi.

content.latin: 44:16 Afferéntur in lætítia et exsultatióne: * adducéntur in templum Regis.
content.english: 44:16 They shall be brought with gladness and rejoicing: * they shall be brought into the temple of the king.

segments.t: Afferéntur in lætítia et exsultatióne: * adducéntur in templum Regis.

content.latin: 44:17 Pro pátribus tuis nati sunt tibi fílii: * constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram.
content.english: 44:17 Instead of thy fathers, sons are born to thee: * thou shalt make them princes over all the earth.

segments.t: Pro pátribus tuis nati sunt tibi fílii: * constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram.

content.latin: 44:18 Mémores erunt nóminis tui: * in omni generatióne et generatiónem.
content.english: 44:18 They shall remember thy name * throughout all generations.

segments.t: Mémores erunt nóminis tui: * in omni generatióne et generatiónem.

content.latin: 44:18 Proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum: * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 44:18 Therefore shall people praise thee for ever; yea, * for ever and ever.

segments.t: Proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum: * et in sǽculum sǽculi.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram: mémores erunt nóminis tui, Dómine.
content.english: Ant. Thou shalt make them princes over all the earth. They shall remember thy name, O Lord.

segments.t: Ant.
Constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram: mémores erunt nóminis tui, Dómine.

content.latin: ℣. In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum.
content.english: ℣. Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth:

segments.t: In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum.

content.latin: ℟. Et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.
content.english: ℟. And their words unto the ends of the world.

segments.t: Et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

segments.t: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

segments.t: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

segments.t: Sed líbera nos a malo.

content.latin: Absolutio. Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Absolution. O Lord Jesus Christ, graciously hear the prayers of Thy servants, and have mercy upon us, Who livest and reignest with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, ever world without end.

segments.t: Absolutio.
Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.
content.english: Benediction. May the Eternal Father bless us with an eternal blessing.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: Incipit liber Ezechiélis Prophétæ
content.english: Lesson from the book of Ezekiel

content.latin: Ezech 1:1-4
content.english: Ezek 1:1-4

segments.t: Ezech 1:1-4

content.latin: 1 Et factum est in trigésimo anno, in quarto, in quinta mensis, cum essem in médio captivórum iuxta flúvium Chobar, apérti sunt cæli, et vidi visiónes Dei.
content.english: 1 Now it came to pass in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth day of the month, when I was in the midst of the captives by the river Chobar, the heavens were opened, and I saw the visions of God.

segments.t: Et factum est in trigésimo anno, in quarto, in quinta mensis, cum essem in médio captivórum iuxta flúvium Chobar, apérti sunt cæli, et vidi visiónes Dei.

content.latin: 2 In quinta mensis, ipse est annus quintus transmigratiónis regis Ióachim,
content.english: 2 On the fifth day of the month, the same was the fifth year of the captivity of king Joachin,

segments.t: In quinta mensis, ipse est annus quintus transmigratiónis regis Ióachim,

content.latin: 3 Factum est verbum Dómini ad Ezechiélem fílium Buzi sacerdótem, in terra Chaldæórum, secus flumen Chobar: et facta est super eum ibi manus Dómini.
content.english: 3 The word of the Lord came to Ezechiel the priest the son of Buzi in the land of the Chaldeans, by the river Chobar: and the hand of the Lord was there upon him.

segments.t: Factum est verbum Dómini ad Ezechiélem fílium Buzi sacerdótem, in terra Chaldæórum, secus flumen Chobar: et facta est super eum ibi manus Dómini.

content.latin: 4 Et vidi, et ecce ventus túrbinis veniébat ab Aquilóne, et nubes magna, et ignis invólvens, et splendor in circúitu eius: et de médio eius, quasi spécies eléctri, id est, de médio ignis:
content.english: 4 And I saw, and behold a whirlwind came out of the north: and a great cloud, and a fire infolding it, and brightness was about it: and out of the midst thereof, that is, out of the midst of the fire, as it were the resemblance of amber.

segments.t: Et vidi, et ecce ventus túrbinis veniébat ab Aquilóne, et nubes magna, et ignis invólvens, et splendor in circúitu eius: et de médio eius, quasi spécies eléctri, id est, de médio ignis:

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Ecce ego mitto vos sicut oves in médio lupórum, dicit Dóminus:
content.english: ℟. Behold, I send you as sheep in the midst of wolves, said the Lord:

segments.t: Ecce ego mitto vos sicut oves in médio lupórum, dicit Dóminus:

content.latin: * Estóte ergo prudéntes sicut serpéntes, et símplices sicut colúmbæ.
content.english: * Be ye, therefore, wise as serpents and simple as doves.

content.latin: ℣. Dum lucem habétis, crédite in lucem, ut fílii lucis sitis.
content.english: ℣. Whilst you have the light, believe in the light, that you may be the children of light.

segments.t: Dum lucem habétis, crédite in lucem, ut fílii lucis sitis.

content.latin: ℟. Estóte ergo prudéntes sicut serpéntes, et símplices sicut colúmbæ.
content.english: ℟. Be ye therefore wise as serpents and simple as doves.

segments.t: Estóte ergo prudéntes sicut serpéntes, et símplices sicut colúmbæ.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.
content.english: Benediction. May the Son, the Sole-begotten, mercifully bless and keep us.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: Ezech 1:5-9
content.english: Ezek 1:5-9

segments.t: Ezech 1:5-9

content.latin: 5 Et in médio eius similitúdo quátuor animálium, et hic aspéctus eórum, similitúdo hóminis in eis.
content.english: 5 And in the midst thereof the likeness of four living creatures: and this was their appearance: there was the likeness of a man in them.

segments.t: Et in médio eius similitúdo quátuor animálium, et hic aspéctus eórum, similitúdo hóminis in eis.

content.latin: 6 Quátuor fácies uni, et quátuor pennæ uni.
content.english: 6 Every one had four faces, and every one four wings.

segments.t: Quátuor fácies uni, et quátuor pennæ uni.

content.latin: 7 Pedes eórum, pedes recti, et planta pedis eórum quasi planta pedis vítuli: et scintíllæ quasi aspéctus æris candéntis.
content.english: 7 Their feet were straight feet, and the sole of their foot was like the sole of a calf's foot, and they sparkled like the appearance of glowing brass.

segments.t: Pedes eórum, pedes recti, et planta pedis eórum quasi planta pedis vítuli: et scintíllæ quasi aspéctus æris candéntis.

content.latin: 8 Et manus hóminis sub pennis eórum, in quátuor pártibus: et fácies et pennas per quátuor partes habébant,
content.english: 8 And they had the hands of a man under their wings on their four sides: and they had faces, and wings on the four sides,

segments.t: Et manus hóminis sub pennis eórum, in quátuor pártibus: et fácies et pennas per quátuor partes habébant,

content.latin: 9 Iunctǽque erant pennæ eórum altérius ad álterum. Non revertebántur cum incéderent, sed unumquódque ante fáciem suam gradiebátur.
content.english: 9 And the wings of one were joined to the wings of another. They turned not when they went: but every one went straight forward.

segments.t: Iunctǽque erant pennæ eórum altérius ad álterum. Non revertebántur cum incéderent, sed unumquódque ante fáciem suam gradiebátur.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Tóllite iugum meum super vos, dicit Dóminus, et díscite a me, quia mitis sum et húmilis corde:
content.english: ℟. Take up my yoke upon you, said the Lord, and learn of me, because I am meek, and humble of heart.

segments.t: Tóllite iugum meum super vos, dicit Dóminus, et díscite a me, quia mitis sum et húmilis corde:

content.latin: * Iugum enim meum suáve est, et onus meum leve.
content.english: * For my yoke is sweet and my burden light.

content.latin: ℣. Et inveniétis réquiem animábus vestris.
content.english: ℣. And you shall find rest to your souls.

segments.t: Et inveniétis réquiem animábus vestris.

content.latin: ℟. Iugum enim meum suáve est, et onus meum leve.
content.english: ℟. For my yoke is sweet and my burden light.

segments.t: Iugum enim meum suáve est, et onus meum leve.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.
content.english: Benediction. May the grace of the Holy Spirit enlighten all our hearts and minds.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: Ezech 1:10-12

segments.t: Ezech 1:10-12

content.latin: 10 Similitúdo autem vultus eórum, fácies hóminis et fácies leónis a dextris ipsórum quátuor, fácies autem bovis a sinístris ipsórum quátuor, et fácies áquilæ désuper ipsórum quátuor.
content.english: 10 And as for the likeness of their faces: there was the face of a man, and the face of a lion on the right side of all the four: and the face of an ox, on the left side of all the four: and the face of an eagle over all the four.

segments.t: Similitúdo autem vultus eórum, fácies hóminis et fácies leónis a dextris ipsórum quátuor, fácies autem bovis a sinístris ipsórum quátuor, et fácies áquilæ désuper ipsórum quátuor.

content.latin: 11 Fácies eórum et pennæ eórum exténtæ désuper: duæ pennæ singulórum iungebántur, et duæ tegébant córpora eórum:
content.english: 11 And their faces, and their wings were stretched upward: two wings of every one were joined, and two covered their bodies:

segments.t: Fácies eórum et pennæ eórum exténtæ désuper: duæ pennæ singulórum iungebántur, et duæ tegébant córpora eórum:

content.latin: 12 Et unumquódque eórum coram fácie sua ambulábat: ubi erat ímpetus spíritus, illuc gradiebántur, nec revertebántur cum ambulárent.
content.english: 12 And every one of them went straight forward: whither the impulse of the spirit was to go, thither they went: and they turned not when they went.

segments.t: Et unumquódque eórum coram fácie sua ambulábat: ubi erat ímpetus spíritus, illuc gradiebántur, nec revertebántur cum ambulárent.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Dum stetéritis ante reges et prǽsides, nolíte cogitáre quómodo aut quid loquámini:
content.english: ℟. But when they shall deliver you up to the judges, take no thought how or what to speak:

segments.t: Dum stetéritis ante reges et prǽsides, nolíte cogitáre quómodo aut quid loquámini:

content.latin: * Dábitur enim vobis in illa hora, quid loquámini.
content.english: * for it shall be given you in that hour what to speak:

content.latin: ℣. Non enim vos estis qui loquímini: sed Spíritus Patris vestri, qui lóquitur in vobis.
content.english: ℣. For it is not you that speak, but the spirit of your Father that speaketh in you.

segments.t: Non enim vos estis qui loquímini: sed Spíritus Patris vestri, qui lóquitur in vobis.

content.latin: ℟. Dábitur enim vobis in illa hora, quid loquámini.
content.english: ℟. For it shall be given you in that hour what to speak.

segments.t: Dábitur enim vobis in illa hora, quid loquámini.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: Psalmus 46 [4]
content.english: Psalm 46 [4]

segments.t: Psalmus 46

content.latin: 46:2 Omnes gentes, pláudite mánibus: * iubiláte Deo in voce exsultatiónis.
content.english: 46:2 O clap your hands, all ye nations: * shout unto God with the voice of joy,

segments.t: Omnes gentes, pláudite mánibus: * iubiláte Deo in voce exsultatiónis.

content.latin: 46:3 Quóniam Dóminus excélsus, terríbilis: * Rex magnus super omnem terram.
content.english: 46:3 For the Lord is high, terrible: * a great king over all the earth.

segments.t: Quóniam Dóminus excélsus, terríbilis: * Rex magnus super omnem terram.

content.latin: 46:4 Subiécit pópulos nobis: * et gentes sub pédibus nostris.
content.english: 46:4 He hath subdued the people under us; * and the nations under our feet.

segments.t: Subiécit pópulos nobis: * et gentes sub pédibus nostris.

content.latin: 46:5 Elégit nobis hereditátem suam: * spéciem Iacob, quam diléxit.
content.english: 46:5 He hath chosen for us his inheritance, * the beauty of Jacob which he hath loved.

content.latin: Matthǽus, qui et Levi, Apóstolus et Evangelísta, Caphárnai cum ad telónium sedéret, a Christo vocátus, statim secútus est ipsum; quem étiam cum réliquis discípulis convívio excépit. Post Christi resurrectiónem, ántequam in provínciam proficiscerétur, quæ ei ad prædicándum obtígerat, primus in Iudǽa, propter eos qui ex circumcisióne credíderant, Evangélium Iesu Christi Hebráice scripsit. Mox in Æthiópiam proféctus, Evangélium prædicávit, ac prædicatiónem multis miráculis confirmávit.
content.english: It came to pass one day at Capernaum, that Christ went forth, and saw a publican, named Levi, sitting at the receipt of custom; and He said unto him: Follow Me. And he left all, rose up, and followed Him. And Levi made Him a great feast in his own house. This Levi is the Apostle and Evangelist Matthew. After that Christ was risen again from the dead, and while he was yet in Judea, before he set forth for that land which had fallen to the lot of his preaching, he wrote the Gospel of Jesus Christ in the Hebrew tongue, for the sake of them of the circumcision who had believed. His was the first written of the four Gospels. Thereafter he went to Ethiopia, and there preached the Gospel, confirming his preaching with many miracles.

content.latin: Illo ígitur in primis miráculo, quo regis fíliam a mórtuis excitávit, regem patrem et uxórem eius cum univérsa província ad Christi fidem convértit. Rege mórtuo, Hírtacus, eius succéssor, cum Iphigeníam, régiam fíliam, vellet sibi dari in matrimónium; Matthǽum, cuius ópera illa virginitátem Deo vóverat et in sancto propósito perseverábat, ad altáre mystérium celebrántem iussit occídi. Qui undécimo caléndas octóbris munus apostólicum martýrii glória cumulávit. Cuius corpus Salérnum translátum, ac póstmodum in ecclésia eius nómine dedicáta, Gregório séptimo summo Pontífice, cónditum, ibídem magno hóminum concúrsu ac pietáte cólitur.
content.english: Of his miracles, the most notable was that he raised the King's daughter from the dead, and thereby brought to believe in Christ the King her father, his wife, and all that region. After that the King was dead, Hirtacus, who came after him, was fain to take his daughter Iphigenia to wife, but by the exhortation of Matthew she had made vow of her maidenhood to God, and stood firm to that holy resolution, for which cause Hirtacus commanded to slay the Apostle at the Altar while he was performing the mystery. He crowned the dignity of the Apostleship with the glory of martyrdom upon the 21 st day of September. His body had been brought to Salerno, where it was afterwards buried in a Church dedicated in his name during the papacy of Gregory VII, and there it is held in great worship and sought to by great gatherings of people.

content.latin: Sancta quátuor animália, quæ prophetíæ spíritu futúra prævidéntur, subtíli narratióne describúntur, cum dícitur: Quátuor fácies uni, et quátuor pennæ uni. Quid per fáciem, nisi notítia; et quid per pennas, nisi volátus exprímitur? Per fáciem quippe unusquísque cognóscitur: per pennas vero in altum ávium córpora sublevántur. Fácies ítaque ad fidem pértinet, penna ad contemplatiónem. Per fidem namque ab omnipoténti Deo cognóscimur, sicut ipse de suis óvibus dicit: Ego sum pastor bonus, et cognósco oves meas, et cognóscunt me meæ. Qui rursus ait: Ego scio quos elégerim. Per contemplatiónem vero, qua super nosmetípsos tóllimur, quasi in áëra levámur.
content.english: The Prophet writeth very minutely touching the four holy living creatures, whom he saw in the spirit as being to come. He saith: “Every one had four faces, and every one had four wings.” What signifieth the face save likeness whereby we are known? or wings, save the power to fly since it is by the face that man is known from man, and by their wings that the birds' bodies are carried up into the air. So the face pertaineth to certitude, and the wings to contemplation. With certitude we are known of God Almighty, Who saith: “I am the Good Shepherd, and know My sheep, and am known of Mine.” John x. 14. And again: “I know whom I have chosen.” xiii. 18. And by contemplation, whereby we rise above ourselves, we as it were fly heavenwards.

content.latin: Céteri Evangelístæ, propter verecúndiam et honórem Matthǽi, noluérunt eum nómine appelláre vulgáto, sed dixérunt, Levi; dúplici quippe vocábulo fuit. Ipse autem Matthǽus (secúndum illud quod dícitur a Salomóne: Iustus accusátor est sui in princípio sermónis; et in álio loco: Dic tu peccáta tua, ut iustificéris) Matthǽum se et publicanum nóminat, ut osténdat legéntibus nullum debére salútem desperáre, si ad melióra convérsus sit, cum ipse de publicáno in Apóstolum sit repénte mutátus.
content.english: The other Evangelists, out of tenderness towards the reputation and honour of Matthew, have abstained from speaking of him as a publican by his ordinary name, and have called him Levi. Both names were his. But Matthew himself, according to what Solomon saith: The just man is the first to accuse himself, Prov. xviii. 17, and again, in another place: Declare thou thy sins that thou mayest be justified, doth plainly call himself Matthew the publican, to show unto his readers that none need be hopeless of salvation if he will but strive to do better, since he himself had been all of a sudden changed from a publican into an Apostle.

content.latin: Arguit in hoc loco Porphýrius, et Iuliánus Augústus, vel imperítiam histórici mentiéntis, vel stultítiam eórum qui statim secúti sint Salvatórem, quasi irrationabíliter quémlibet vocántem hóminem sint secúti; cum tantæ virtútes tántaque signa præcésserint, quæ Apóstolos, ántequam créderent, vidísse non dubium est. Certe fulgor ipse et maiéstas Divinitátis occúltæ, quæ étiam in humána fácie relucébat, ex primo ad se vidéntes tráhere póterat aspéctu. Si enim in magnéte lápide et súccinis hæc esse vis dícitur, ut ánulos et stípulam et festúcas sibi cópulent; quanto magis Dóminus ómnium creaturárum ad se tráhere póterat, quos vocábat?
content.english: Porphyry and the Emperor Julian (the Apostate) will have it that the account of this call of Matthew is either a stupid blunder on the part of a lying writer, or else that it showeth what fools they were who followed the Saviour, to go senselessly after any one who called them. But there can be no doubt that before the Apostles believed they had considered the great signs and works of power which had gone before. Moreover, the glory and majesty of the hidden God, which shone somewhat through the Face of the Man Christ Jesus, were enough to draw them which gazed thereon, even at first sight. For if there be in a stone a magnetic power which can make rings and straws and rods come and cleave thereunto, how much more must not the Lord of all creatures have been able to draw unto Himself them whom He called?

content.latin: Et factum est, discumbénte eo in domo, ecce multi publicáni et peccatóres veniéntes discumbébant cum Iesu. Vidébant publicanum, a peccátis ad melióra convérsum, locum invenísse pœniténtiæ; et ob id étiam ipsi non despérant salútem. Neque vero in pristínis vítiis permanéntes véniunt ad Iesum, ut pharisǽi et scribæ múrmurant, sed pœniténtiam agéntes, ut sequens Dómini sermo signíficat, dicens: Misericórdiam volo, et non sacrifícium; non enim veni vocáre iustos, sed peccatóres. Ibat autem Dóminus ad convívia peccatórum, ut occasiónem habéret docéndi, et spirituáles invitatóribus suis præbéret cibos.
content.english: And it came to pass, as Jesus sat at meat in the house, behold, many publicans and sinners came and sat down with Him. They saw how that a publican who had turned to better things had found a place of repentance, and therefore they also hoped for salvation. It was not, as the Scribes and Pharisees complained, sinners clinging to their sinfulness who came to Jesus, but sinners repenting, as indeed appeareth from the next words of the Lord, where He saith: I will have mercy and not sacrifice; for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance. The Lord went to eat with sinners to the end that He might have occasion to teach, and to break spiritual bread unto them which bade Him.

content.english: 148:1 Praise ye the Lord from the heavens * praise ye him in the high places.

segments.t: Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.

content.latin: 148:2 Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes eius.
content.english: 148:2 Praise ye him, all his angels: * praise ye him, all his hosts.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes eius.

content.latin: 148:3 Laudáte eum, sol et luna: * laudáte eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.
content.english: 148:3 Praise ye him, O sun and moon: * praise him, all ye stars and light.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, sol et luna: * laudáte eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.

content.latin: 148:4 Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.
content.english: 148:4 Praise him, ye heavens of heavens: * and let all the waters that are above the heavens, praise the name of the Lord.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.

content.latin: 148:5 Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.
content.english: 148:5 For he spoke, and they were made: * he commanded, and they were created.

segments.t: Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.

content.latin: 148:6 Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.
content.english: 148:6 He hath established them for ever, and for ages of ages: * he hath made a decree, and it shall not pass away.

segments.t: Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.

content.latin: 148:7 Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.
content.english: 148:7 Praise the Lord from the earth, * ye dragons, and all ye deeps:

segments.t: Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.

content.english: 148:8 Fire, hail, snow, ice, stormy winds * which fulfill his word:

segments.t: Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum: * quæ fáciunt verbum eius:

content.latin: 148:9 Montes, et omnes colles: * ligna fructífera, et omnes cedri.
content.english: 148:9 Mountains and all hills, * fruitful trees and all cedars:

segments.t: Montes, et omnes colles: * ligna fructífera, et omnes cedri.

content.latin: 148:10 Béstiæ, et univérsa pécora: * serpéntes, et vólucres pennátæ:
content.english: 148:10 Beasts and all cattle: * serpents and feathered fowls:

segments.t: Béstiæ, et univérsa pécora: * serpéntes, et vólucres pennátæ:

content.english: 148:11 Kings of the earth and all people: * princes and all judges of the earth:

segments.t: Reges terræ, et omnes pópuli: * príncipes, et omnes iúdices terræ.

content.english: 148:12 Young men and maidens: let the old with the younger, praise the name of the Lord: * For his name alone is exalted.

segments.t: Iúvenes, et vírgines: senes cum iunióribus laudent nomen Dómini: * quia exaltátum est nomen eius solíus.

content.latin: 148:14 Conféssio eius super cælum et terram: * et exaltávit cornu pópuli sui.

segments.t: Conféssio eius super cælum et terram: * et exaltávit cornu pópuli sui.

content.english: Brothers: Now therefore you are no more strangers and foreigners; but you are fellow citizens with the saints, and the domestics of God, built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone.

content.latin: Exsúltet orbis gáudiis:
content.english: Now let the earth with joy resound,

content.latin: Cælum resúltet láudibus:
content.english: And heaven the chant re-echo round;

content.latin: Apostolórum glóriam
content.english: Nor heaven nor earth too high can raise

content.latin: Tellus et astra cóncinunt.
content.english: The great Apostles' glorious praise.

content.latin: Vos sæculórum iúdices,
content.english: O ye who, throned in glory dread,

content.latin: Et vera mundi lúmina:
content.english: Shall judge the living and the dead,

content.latin: Votis precámur córdium,
content.english: Lights of the world forevermore!

content.latin: Audíte voces súpplicum.
content.english: To you the suppliant prayer we pour.

content.latin: Qui templa cæli cláuditis,
content.english: Ye close the sacred gates on high;

content.latin: Serásque verbo sólvitis,
content.english: At your command apart they fly:

content.latin: Nos a reátu nóxios
content.english: Oh! loose for us the guilty chain

content.latin: Solvi iubéte, quǽsumus.
content.english: We strive to break, and strive in vain.

content.latin: Præcépta quorum prótinus
content.english: Sickness and health your voice obey;

content.latin: Languor salúsque séntiunt:
content.english: At your command they go or stay:

content.latin: Sanáte mentes lánguidas:
content.english: From sin's disease our souls restore;

content.latin: Augéte nos virtútibus.
content.english: In good confirm us more and more.

content.latin: Ut, cum redíbit árbiter
content.english: So when the world is at its end,

content.latin: In fine Christus sǽculi,
content.english: And Christ to judgement shall descend,

content.latin: Nos sempitérni gáudii
content.english: May we be called those joys to see

content.latin: Concédat esse cómpotes.
content.english: Prepared from all eternity.

content.latin: Patri, simúlque Fílio,
content.english: Praise to the Father, with the Son,

content.latin: Tibíque Sancte Spíritus,
content.english: And Holy Spirit, Three in One;

content.latin: Sicut fuit, sit iúgiter
content.english: As ever was in ages past,

content.latin: Sæclum per omne glória.
content.english: And so shall be while ages last.

content.english: Amen.

content.latin: Sancti Thomæ a Villa Nova, ex Eremitárum sancti Augustíni Ordine, Epíscopi Valentíni et Confessóris; cuius dies natális recólitur sexto Idus Septémbris.
content.english: Upon the same 22nd day of September, were born into the better life:

content.latin: Sedúni, in Gállia, in loco Agáuno, natális sanctórum Mártyrum Thebæórum Maurítii, Exsupérii, Cándidi, Victóris, Innocéntii et Vitális, cum Sóciis eiúsdem legiónis; qui, sub Maximiáno, pro Christo necáti, gloriósa passióne mundum illustrárunt.
content.english: At Sion, in Switzerland, the holy martyrs of the Theban Legion Maurice, Exuperius, Candidus, Victor, Innocent, Vitalis, and their Comrades, who were massacred for Christ's sake under the Emperor Maximian, and have enlightened the whole world by the glory of their passion.

content.latin: Romæ pássio sanctárum Vírginum et Mártyrum Dignæ et Eméritæ, sub Valeriáno et Galliéno; quarum relíquiæ in Ecclésia sancti Marcélli asservántur.
content.english: At Rome, under the Emperors Valerian and Gallienus, the holy Virgins Digna and Emerita, both martyrs. Their relics are kept in the Church of St. Marcellus.

content.latin: Ratisbónæ, in Bavária, sancti Emmerámi, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui, ut álios liberáret, mortem sævíssimam, Christi causa, patiénter súbiit.
content.english: At Chartres, the holy martyr Jonah, a Priest, who came into Gaul along with holy Denis, and was, by command of the Prefect Julian, flogged and beheaded.

content.latin: Apud pagum Castrénsium sancti Ionæ, Presbýteri et Mártyris; qui, cum sancto Dionýsio proféctus in Gálliam, ibídem, Iuliáni Præfécti iussu verbéribus cæsus, gládio martýrium consummávit.
content.english: At Regensburg, in Bavaria, (in the seventh century,) the holy martyr Emmeram, the Bishop who, in order that he might deliver others, patiently submitted to a most cruel death for Christ's sake.

content.latin: Antinoópoli, in Ægýpto, sanctæ Iráidis, Vírginis Alexandrínæ, et Sociórum Mártyrum. Ipsa Virgo, cum esset ad hauriéndam e próximo fonte aquam egréssa, et navim vidísset Confessóribus Christi onústam, prótinus, relícta hýdria, se illis adiúnxit, ac, simul cum iis in urbem ducta, prima ómnium, post multa supplícia, cápite cæsa est; deínde Presbýteri, Diáconi, et Vírgines, aliíque omnes eódem mortis génere consúmpti sunt.
content.english: At Antinoopolis, in Egypt, the holy martyrs Irais, a Virgin of Alexandria, and her Companions. She was gone out to draw water from a well near by when she saw a ship full of confessors of Christ, and thereupon she forthwith left her water-pot and joined them, and was brought along with them into the city, where she first of all, after many torments, was beheaded, and then all the rest, of whom some were Priests, Deacons, or Virgins, were put to the same death.

content.latin: Romæ sancti Felícis Papæ Quarti, qui pro fide cathólica plúrimum laborávit.
content.english: At Meaux, blessed Sanctinus, a disciple of holy Denys the Areopagite, who consecrated him Bishop of that city, where he was the first to preach the Gospel.

content.latin: Apud civitátem Meldénsem beáti Sanctíni Epíscopi, qui fuit discípulus sancti Dionýsii Areopagítæ; et, eiúsdem civitátis Epíscopus ab eo consecrátus, primus illic Evangélium prædicávit.
content.english: In the country of Coutances, (in the sixth century,) the holy Confessor Lauto, Bishop (of that see.)

content.latin: In território Constantiénsi, in Gállia, sancti Lautónis Epíscopi.
content.english: In Poitou, (in the fifth century,) the holy Priest Florence.

content.latin: In monte Glonna, ad Lígerim flumen, in Gállia, sancti Floréntii Presbýteri.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Dirígere et sanctificáre, régere et gubernáre dignáre, Dómine Deus, Rex cæli et terræ, hódie corda et córpora nostra, sensus, sermónes et actus nostros in lege tua, et in opéribus mandatórum tuórum: ut hic et in ætérnum, te auxiliánte, salvi et líberi esse mereámur, Salvátor mundi: Qui vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: O Lord, Almighty God, King of heaven and earth, Saviour of the world, bless, lead, rule and govern our hearts and bodies, our senses, words and deeds today, following thy law and commandments, that here and for eternity with thy help we shall be saved in freedom. Who livest and reignest, world without end.

content.latin: 26:1 Dóminus illuminátio mea, et salus mea, * quem timébo?
content.english: 26:1 The Lord is my light and my salvation, * whom shall I fear?

segments.t: Dóminus illuminátio mea, et salus mea, * quem timébo?

content.latin: 26:1 Dóminus protéctor vitæ meæ, * a quo trepidábo?
content.english: 26:1 The Lord is the protector of my life: * of whom shall I be afraid?

segments.t: Dóminus protéctor vitæ meæ, * a quo trepidábo?

content.latin: 26:2 Dum apprópiant super me nocéntes, * ut edant carnes meas:
content.english: 26:2 Whilst the wicked draw near against me, * to eat my flesh.

segments.t: Dum apprópiant super me nocéntes, * ut edant carnes meas:

content.latin: 26:2 Qui tríbulant me inimíci mei, * ipsi infirmáti sunt, et cecidérunt.
content.english: 26:2 My enemies that trouble me, * have themselves been weakened, and have fallen.

segments.t: Qui tríbulant me inimíci mei, * ipsi infirmáti sunt, et cecidérunt.

content.latin: 26:3 Si consístant advérsum me castra, * non timébit cor meum.
content.english: 26:3 If armies in camp should stand together against me, * my heart shall not fear.

segments.t: Si consístant advérsum me castra, * non timébit cor meum.

content.latin: 26:3 Si exsúrgat advérsum me prǽlium, * in hoc ego sperábo.
content.english: 26:3 If a battle should rise up against me, * in this will I be confident.

segments.t: Si exsúrgat advérsum me prǽlium, * in hoc ego sperábo.

content.latin: 26:4 Unam pétii a Dómino, hanc requíram, * ut inhábitem in domo Dómini ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ:
content.english: 26:4 One thing I have asked of the Lord, this will I seek after; * that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life.

segments.t: Unam pétii a Dómino, hanc requíram, * ut inhábitem in domo Dómini ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ:

content.latin: 26:4 Ut vídeam voluptátem Dómini, * et vísitem templum eius.
content.english: 26:4 That I may see the delight of the Lord, * and may visit his temple.

segments.t: Ut vídeam voluptátem Dómini, * et vísitem templum eius.

content.latin: 26:5 Quóniam abscóndit me in tabernáculo suo: * in die malórum protéxit me in abscóndito tabernáculi sui.
content.english: 26:5 For he hath hidden me in his tabernacle; * in the day of evils, he hath protected me in the secret place of his tabernacle.

segments.t: Quóniam abscóndit me in tabernáculo suo: * in die malórum protéxit me in abscóndito tabernáculi sui.

content.latin: 26:6 In petra exaltávit me: * et nunc exaltávit caput meum super inimícos meos.
content.english: 26:6 He hath exalted me upon a rock: * and now he hath lifted up my head above my enemies.

segments.t: In petra exaltávit me: * et nunc exaltávit caput meum super inimícos meos.

content.latin: 26:6 Circuívi, et immolávi in tabernáculo eius hóstiam vociferatiónis: * cantábo, et psalmum dicam Dómino.
content.english: 26:6 I have gone round, and have offered up in his tabernacle a sacrifice of jubilation: * I will sing, and recite a psalm to the Lord.

segments.t: Circuívi, et immolávi in tabernáculo eius hóstiam vociferatiónis: * cantábo, et psalmum dicam Dómino.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

Psalmus 26(7-14)

content.latin: 26:7 Exáudi, Dómine, vocem meam, qua clamávi ad te: * miserére mei, et exáudi me.
content.english: 26:7 Hear, O Lord, my voice, with which I have cried to thee: * have mercy on me and hear me.

segments.t: Exáudi, Dómine, vocem meam, qua clamávi ad te: * miserére mei, et exáudi me.

content.latin: 26:8 Tibi dixit cor meum, exquisívit te fácies mea: * fáciem tuam, Dómine, requíram.
content.english: 26:8 My heart hath said to thee: My face hath sought thee: * thy face, O Lord, will I still seek.

segments.t: Tibi dixit cor meum, exquisívit te fácies mea: * fáciem tuam, Dómine, requíram.

content.latin: 26:9 Ne avértas fáciem tuam a me: * ne declínes in ira a servo tuo.
content.english: 26:9 Turn not away thy face from me; * decline not in thy wrath from thy servant.

segments.t: Ne avértas fáciem tuam a me: * ne declínes in ira a servo tuo.

content.latin: 26:9 Adiútor meus esto: * ne derelínquas me, neque despícias me, Deus, salutáris meus.
content.english: 26:9 Be thou my helper, * forsake me not; do not thou despise me, O God my Saviour.

segments.t: Adiútor meus esto: * ne derelínquas me, neque despícias me, Deus, salutáris meus.

content.latin: 26:10 Quóniam pater meus, et mater mea dereliquérunt me: * Dóminus autem assúmpsit me.
content.english: 26:10 For my father and my mother have left me: * but the Lord hath taken me up.

segments.t: Quóniam pater meus, et mater mea dereliquérunt me: * Dóminus autem assúmpsit me.

content.latin: 26:11 Legem pone mihi, Dómine, in via tua: * et dírige me in sémitam rectam propter inimícos meos.
content.english: 26:11 Set me, O Lord, a law in thy way, * and guide me in the right path, because of my enemies.

segments.t: Legem pone mihi, Dómine, in via tua: * et dírige me in sémitam rectam propter inimícos meos.

content.latin: 26:12 Ne tradíderis me in ánimas tribulántium me: * quóniam insurrexérunt in me testes iníqui, et mentíta est iníquitas sibi.
content.english: 26:12 Deliver me not over to the will of them that trouble me; * for unjust witnesses have risen up against me; and iniquity hath lied to itself.

segments.t: Ne tradíderis me in ánimas tribulántium me: * quóniam insurrexérunt in me testes iníqui, et mentíta est iníquitas sibi.

content.latin: 26:13 Credo vidére bona Dómini * in terra vivéntium.
content.english: 26:13 I believe to see the good things of the Lord * in the land of the living.

segments.t: Credo vidére bona Dómini * in terra vivéntium.

content.latin: 26:14 Exspécta Dóminum, viríliter age: * et confortétur cor tuum, et sústine Dóminum.
content.english: 26:14 Expect the Lord, do manfully, * and let thy heart take courage, and wait thou for the Lord.

segments.t: Exspécta Dóminum, viríliter age: * et confortétur cor tuum, et sústine Dóminum.

content.english: Psalm 27 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 27

content.latin: 27:1 Ad te, Dómine, clamábo, Deus meus, ne síleas a me: * nequándo táceas a me, et assimilábor descendéntibus in lacum.
content.english: 27:1 Unto thee will I cry, O Lord: my God, be not thou silent to me: * lest if thou be silent to me, I become like them that go down into the pit.

segments.t: Ad te, Dómine, clamábo, Deus meus, ne síleas a me: * nequándo táceas a me, et assimilábor descendéntibus in lacum.

content.latin: 27:2 Exáudi, Dómine, vocem deprecatiónis meæ dum oro ad te: * dum extóllo manus meas ad templum sanctum tuum.
content.english: 27:2 Hear, O Lord, the voice of my supplication, when I pray to thee; * when I lift up my hands to thy holy temple.

segments.t: Exáudi, Dómine, vocem deprecatiónis meæ dum oro ad te: * dum extóllo manus meas ad templum sanctum tuum.

content.latin: 27:3 Ne simul trahas me cum peccatóribus: * et cum operántibus iniquitátem ne perdas me.
content.english: 27:3 Draw me not away together with the wicked; * and with the workers of iniquity destroy me not:

segments.t: Ne simul trahas me cum peccatóribus: * et cum operántibus iniquitátem ne perdas me.

content.latin: 27:3 Qui loquúntur pacem cum próximo suo, * mala autem in córdibus eórum.
content.english: 27:3 Who speak peace with their neighbour, * but evils are in their hearts.

segments.t: Qui loquúntur pacem cum próximo suo, * mala autem in córdibus eórum.

content.latin: 27:4 Da illis secúndum ópera eórum, * et secúndum nequítiam adinventiónum ipsórum.
content.english: 27:4 Give them according to their works, * and according to the wickedness of their inventions.

segments.t: Da illis secúndum ópera eórum, * et secúndum nequítiam adinventiónum ipsórum.

content.latin: 27:4 Secúndum ópera mánuum eórum tríbue illis: * redde retributiónem eórum ipsis.
content.english: 27:4 According to the works of their hands give thou to them: * render to them their reward.

segments.t: Secúndum ópera mánuum eórum tríbue illis: * redde retributiónem eórum ipsis.

content.latin: 27:5 Quóniam non intellexérunt ópera Dómini, et in ópera mánuum eius * déstrues illos, et non ædificábis eos.
content.english: 27:5 Because they have not understood the works of the Lord, and the operations of his hands: * thou shalt destroy them, and shalt not build them up.

segments.t: Quóniam non intellexérunt ópera Dómini, et in ópera mánuum eius * déstrues illos, et non ædificábis eos.

content.latin: 27:6 Benedíctus Dóminus: * quóniam exaudívit vocem deprecatiónis meæ.
content.english: 27:6 Blessed be the Lord, * for he hath heard the voice of my supplication.

segments.t: Benedíctus Dóminus: * quóniam exaudívit vocem deprecatiónis meæ.

content.latin: 27:7 Dóminus adiútor meus, et protéctor meus: * in ipso sperávit cor meum, et adiútus sum.
content.english: 27:7 The Lord is my helper and my protector: * in him hath my heart confided, and I have been helped.

segments.t: Dóminus adiútor meus, et protéctor meus: * in ipso sperávit cor meum, et adiútus sum.

content.latin: 27:7 Et reflóruit caro mea: * et ex voluntáte mea confitébor ei.
content.english: 27:7 And my flesh hath flourished again, * and with my will I will give praise to him.

segments.t: Et reflóruit caro mea: * et ex voluntáte mea confitébor ei.

content.latin: 27:8 Dóminus fortitúdo plebis suæ: * et protéctor salvatiónum Christi sui est.
content.english: 27:8 The Lord is the strength of his people, * and the protector of the salvation of his anointed.

segments.t: Dóminus fortitúdo plebis suæ: * et protéctor salvatiónum Christi sui est.

content.latin: 27:9 Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, et bénedic hereditáti tuæ: * et rege eos, et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.
content.english: 27:9 Save, O Lord, thy people, and bless thy inheritance: * and rule them and exalt them for ever.

segments.t: Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, et bénedic hereditáti tuæ: * et rege eos, et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.

content.latin: 30:2 In te, Dómine, sperávi, non confúndar in ætérnum: * in iustítia tua líbera me.
content.english: 30:2 In thee, O Lord, have I hoped, let me never be confounded: * deliver me in thy justice.

content.english: 30:3 Bow down thy ear to me: * make haste to deliver me.

segments.t: Inclína ad me aurem tuam, * accélera ut éruas me.

content.latin: 30:3 Esto mihi in Deum protectórem, et in domum refúgii: * ut salvum me fácias.
content.english: 30:3 Be thou unto me a God, a protector, and a house of refuge, * to save me.

segments.t: Esto mihi in Deum protectórem, et in domum refúgii: * ut salvum me fácias.

content.latin: 30:4 Quóniam fortitúdo mea, et refúgium meum es tu: * et propter nomen tuum dedúces me, et enútries me.
content.english: 30:4 For thou art my strength and my refuge; * and for thy name’s sake thou wilt lead me, and nourish me.

segments.t: Quóniam fortitúdo mea, et refúgium meum es tu: * et propter nomen tuum dedúces me, et enútries me.

content.latin: 30:5 Edúces me de láqueo hoc, quem abscondérunt mihi: * quóniam tu es protéctor meus.
content.english: 30:5 Thou wilt bring me out of this snare, which they have hidden for me: * for thou art my protector.

segments.t: Edúces me de láqueo hoc, quem abscondérunt mihi: * quóniam tu es protéctor meus.

content.latin: 30:6 In manus tuas comméndo spíritum meum: * redemísti me, Dómine, Deus veritátis.
content.english: 30:6 Into thy hands I commend my spirit: * thou hast redeemed me, O Lord, the God of truth.

segments.t: In manus tuas comméndo spíritum meum: * redemísti me, Dómine, Deus veritátis.

content.latin: 30:7 Odísti observántes vanitátes, * supervácue.
content.english: 30:7 Thou hast hated them that regard vanities, * to no purpose.

segments.t: Odísti observántes vanitátes, * supervácue.

content.latin: 30:7 Ego autem in Dómino sperávi: * exsultábo, et lætábor in misericórdia tua.
content.english: 30:7 But I have hoped in the Lord: * I will be glad and rejoice in thy mercy.

segments.t: Ego autem in Dómino sperávi: * exsultábo, et lætábor in misericórdia tua.

content.latin: 30:8 Quóniam respexísti humilitátem meam, * salvásti de necessitátibus ánimam meam.
content.english: 30:8 For thou hast regarded my humility, * thou hast saved my soul out of distresses.

segments.t: Quóniam respexísti humilitátem meam, * salvásti de necessitátibus ánimam meam.

content.latin: 30:9 Nec conclusísti me in mánibus inimíci: * statuísti in loco spatióso pedes meos.
content.english: 30:9 And thou hast not shut me up in the hands of the enemy: * thou hast set my feet in a spacious place.

segments.t: Nec conclusísti me in mánibus inimíci: * statuísti in loco spatióso pedes meos.

content.english: Psalm 31 [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 31

content.latin: 31:1 Beáti quorum remíssæ sunt iniquitátes: * et quorum tecta sunt peccáta.
content.english: 31:1 Blessed are those whose iniquities are forgiven * and whose sins are covered.

segments.t: Beáti quorum remíssæ sunt iniquitátes: * et quorum tecta sunt peccáta.

content.latin: 31:2 Beátus vir, cui non imputávit Dóminus peccátum, * nec est in spíritu eius dolus.
content.english: 31:2 Blessed is the man to whom the Lord hath not imputed sin, * and in whose spirit there is no guile.

segments.t: Beátus vir, cui non imputávit Dóminus peccátum, * nec est in spíritu eius dolus.

content.latin: 31:3 Quóniam tácui, inveteravérunt ossa mea, * dum clamárem tota die.
content.english: 31:3 Because I was silent my bones grew old; * whilst I cried out all the day long.

segments.t: Quóniam tácui, inveteravérunt ossa mea, * dum clamárem tota die.

content.latin: 31:4 Quóniam die ac nocte graváta est super me manus tua: * convérsus sum in ærúmna mea, dum confígitur spina.
content.english: 31:4 For day and night thy hand was heavy upon me: * I am turned in my anguish, whilst the thorn is fastened.

segments.t: Quóniam die ac nocte graváta est super me manus tua: * convérsus sum in ærúmna mea, dum confígitur spina.

content.latin: 31:5 Delíctum meum cógnitum tibi feci: * et iniustítiam meam non abscóndi.
content.english: 31:5 I have acknowledged my sin to thee, * and my injustice I have not concealed.

segments.t: Delíctum meum cógnitum tibi feci: * et iniustítiam meam non abscóndi.

content.latin: 31:5 Dixi: Confitébor advérsum me iniustítiam meam Dómino: * et tu remisísti impietátem peccáti mei.
content.english: 31:5 I said I will confess against myself my injustice to the Lord: * and thou hast forgiven the wickedness of my sin.

segments.t: Dixi: Confitébor advérsum me iniustítiam meam Dómino: * et tu remisísti impietátem peccáti mei.

content.latin: 31:6 Pro hac orábit ad te omnis sanctus, * in témpore opportúno.
content.english: 31:6 For this shall every one that is holy pray to thee * in a seasonable time.

segments.t: Pro hac orábit ad te omnis sanctus, * in témpore opportúno.

content.latin: 31:6 Verúmtamen in dilúvio aquárum multárum, * ad eum non approximábunt.
content.english: 31:6 And yet in a flood of many waters, * they shall not come nigh unto him.

segments.t: Verúmtamen in dilúvio aquárum multárum, * ad eum non approximábunt.

content.latin: 31:7 Tu es refúgium meum a tribulatióne, quæ circúmdedit me: * exsultátio mea, érue me a circumdántibus me.
content.english: 31:7 Thou art my refuge from the trouble which hath encompassed me: * my joy, deliver me from them that surround me.

segments.t: Tu es refúgium meum a tribulatióne, quæ circúmdedit me: * exsultátio mea, érue me a circumdántibus me.

content.latin: 31:8 Intelléctum tibi dabo, et ínstruam te in via hac, qua gradiéris: * firmábo super te óculos meos.
content.english: 31:8 I will give thee understanding, and I will instruct thee in this way, in which thou shalt go: * I will fix my eyes upon thee.

segments.t: Intelléctum tibi dabo, et ínstruam te in via hac, qua gradiéris: * firmábo super te óculos meos.

content.latin: 31:9 Nolíte fíeri sicut equus et mulus, * quibus non est intelléctus.
content.english: 31:9 Do not become like the horse and the mule, * who have no understanding.

segments.t: Nolíte fíeri sicut equus et mulus, * quibus non est intelléctus.

content.latin: 31:9 In camo et freno maxíllas eórum constrínge, * qui non appróximant ad te.
content.english: 31:9 With bit and bridle bind fast their jaws, * who come not near unto thee.

segments.t: In camo et freno maxíllas eórum constrínge, * qui non appróximant ad te.

content.latin: 31:10 Multa flagélla peccatóris, * sperántem autem in Dómino misericórdia circúmdabit.
content.english: 31:10 Many are the scourges of the sinner, * but mercy shall encompass him that hopeth in the Lord.

segments.t: Multa flagélla peccatóris, * sperántem autem in Dómino misericórdia circúmdabit.

content.latin: 31:11 Lætámini in Dómino et exsultáte, iusti, * et gloriámini, omnes recti corde.
content.english: 31:11 Be glad in the Lord, and rejoice, ye just, * and glory, all ye right of heart.

segments.t: Lætámini in Dómino et exsultáte, iusti, * et gloriámini, omnes recti corde.

Psalmus 32(1-11)

content.latin: 32:1 Exsultáte, iusti, in Dómino: * rectos decet collaudátio.
content.english: 32:1 Rejoice in the Lord, O ye just: * praise becometh the upright.

segments.t: Exsultáte, iusti, in Dómino: * rectos decet collaudátio.

content.latin: 32:2 Confitémini Dómino in cíthara: * in psaltério decem chordárum psállite illi.
content.english: 32:2 Give praise to the Lord on the harp; * sing to him with the psaltery, the instrument of ten strings.

segments.t: Confitémini Dómino in cíthara: * in psaltério decem chordárum psállite illi.

content.latin: 32:3 Cantáte ei cánticum novum: * bene psállite ei in vociferatióne.
content.english: 32:3 Sing to him a new canticle, * sing well unto him with a loud noise.

segments.t: Cantáte ei cánticum novum: * bene psállite ei in vociferatióne.

content.latin: 32:4 Quia rectum est verbum Dómini, * et ómnia ópera eius in fide.
content.english: 32:4 For the word of the Lord is right, * and all his works are done with faithfulness.

segments.t: Quia rectum est verbum Dómini, * et ómnia ópera eius in fide.

content.latin: 32:5 Díligit misericórdiam et iudícium: * misericórdia Dómini plena est terra.
content.english: 32:5 He loveth mercy and judgment; * the earth is full of the mercy of the Lord.

segments.t: Díligit misericórdiam et iudícium: * misericórdia Dómini plena est terra.

content.latin: 32:6 Verbo Dómini cæli firmáti sunt: * et spíritu oris eius omnis virtus eórum.
content.english: 32:6 By the word of the Lord the heavens were established; * and all the power of them by the spirit of his mouth:

segments.t: Verbo Dómini cæli firmáti sunt: * et spíritu oris eius omnis virtus eórum.

content.latin: 32:7 Cóngregans sicut in utre aquas maris: * ponens in thesáuris abýssos.
content.english: 32:7 Gathering together the waters of the sea, as in a vessel; * laying up the depths in storehouses.

segments.t: Cóngregans sicut in utre aquas maris: * ponens in thesáuris abýssos.

content.latin: 32:8 Tímeat Dóminum omnis terra: * ab eo autem commoveántur omnes inhabitántes orbem.
content.english: 32:8 Let all the earth fear the Lord, * and let all the inhabitants of the world be in awe of him.

segments.t: Tímeat Dóminum omnis terra: * ab eo autem commoveántur omnes inhabitántes orbem.

content.latin: 32:9 Quóniam ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.
content.english: 32:9 For he spoke and they were made: * he commanded and they were created.

segments.t: Quóniam ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.

content.latin: 32:10 Dóminus díssipat consília géntium: * réprobat autem cogitatiónes populórum, et réprobat consília príncipum.
content.english: 32:10 The Lord bringeth to nought the counsels of nations; * and he rejecteth the devices of people, and casteth away the counsels of princes.

segments.t: Dóminus díssipat consília géntium: * réprobat autem cogitatiónes populórum, et réprobat consília príncipum.

content.latin: 32:11 Consílium autem Dómini in ætérnum manet: * cogitatiónes cordis eius in generatióne et generatiónem.
content.english: 32:11 But the counsel of the Lord standeth for ever: * the thoughts of his heart to all generations.

segments.t: Consílium autem Dómini in ætérnum manet: * cogitatiónes cordis eius in generatióne et generatiónem.

content.latin: 32:12 Beáta gens, cuius est Dóminus, Deus eius: * pópulus, quem elégit in hereditátem sibi.
content.english: 32:12 Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord: * the people whom he hath chosen for his inheritance.

segments.t: Beáta gens, cuius est Dóminus, Deus eius: * pópulus, quem elégit in hereditátem sibi.

content.latin: 32:13 De cælo respéxit Dóminus: * vidit omnes fílios hóminum.
content.english: 32:13 The Lord hath looked from heaven: * he hath beheld all the sons of men.

segments.t: De cælo respéxit Dóminus: * vidit omnes fílios hóminum.

content.latin: 32:14 De præparáto habitáculo suo * respéxit super omnes, qui hábitant terram.
content.english: 32:14 From his habitation which he hath prepared, * he hath looked upon all that dwell on the earth.

segments.t: De præparáto habitáculo suo * respéxit super omnes, qui hábitant terram.

content.latin: 32:15 Qui finxit sigillátim corda eórum: * qui intéllegit ómnia ópera eórum.
content.english: 32:15 He who hath made the hearts of every one of them: * who understandeth all their works.

segments.t: Qui finxit sigillátim corda eórum: * qui intéllegit ómnia ópera eórum.

content.latin: 32:16 Non salvátur rex per multam virtútem: * et gigas non salvábitur in multitúdine virtútis suæ.
content.english: 32:16 The king is not saved by a great army: * nor shall the giant be saved by his own great strength.

segments.t: Non salvátur rex per multam virtútem: * et gigas non salvábitur in multitúdine virtútis suæ.

content.latin: 32:17 Fallax equus ad salútem: * in abundántia autem virtútis suæ non salvábitur.
content.english: 32:17 Vain is the horse for safety: * neither shall he be saved by the abundance of his strength.

segments.t: Fallax equus ad salútem: * in abundántia autem virtútis suæ non salvábitur.

content.latin: 32:18 Ecce, óculi Dómini super metuéntes eum: * et in eis, qui sperant super misericórdia eius:
content.english: 32:18 Behold the eyes of the Lord are on them that fear him: * and on them that hope in his mercy.

segments.t: Ecce, óculi Dómini super metuéntes eum: * et in eis, qui sperant super misericórdia eius:

content.latin: 32:19 Ut éruat a morte ánimas eórum: * et alat eos in fame.
content.english: 32:19 To deliver their souls from death; * and feed them in famine.

segments.t: Ut éruat a morte ánimas eórum: * et alat eos in fame.

content.latin: 32:20 Ánima nostra sústinet Dóminum: * quóniam adiútor et protéctor noster est.
content.english: 32:20 Our soul waiteth for the Lord: * for he is our helper and protector.

segments.t: Ánima nostra sústinet Dóminum: * quóniam adiútor et protéctor noster est.

content.latin: 32:21 Quia in eo lætábitur cor nostrum: * et in nómine sancto eius sperávimus.
content.english: 32:21 For in him our heart shall rejoice: * and in his holy name we have trusted.

segments.t: Quia in eo lætábitur cor nostrum: * et in nómine sancto eius sperávimus.

content.latin: 32:22 Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos: * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.
content.english: 32:22 Let thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us, * as we have hoped in thee.

segments.t: Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos: * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.
